results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 55 aligned outline summaries state the controlling idea of their spec paragraph, in spec order; the five callouts are unmatched front matter.

Only Evaluating Recommendations ¶2 was marked two_ideas. Its spec controlling idea (p34) is one idea, what to measure offline, and the draft presents ANN recall as one more offline metric ('an engineering metric in its own right'); the paragraph matches its spec unit.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim R1-R6 (scene, surfaces, why-listings-differ -> R1; methods, architecture sources, cold start -> R2; filter, freshness, Hearthly duplicates -> R3; re-ranker, policy, feedback, evaluation, rebuild -> R4; privacy -> R5; Chief Architect's view -> R6).

Each table, figure, case and quotation has a sentence, caption or column that says what it shows (scene table -> ¶4; methods table -> lead sentence; each dated case ends on its lesson; filter table -> shared status rule; guardrail table's 'What it protects'; rebuild table -> 'The last row...'; Felix's quotation is itself the lesson).

results.quote: Recommendations look like a feature owned by a product squad. At group scale they are a **platform capability with brand-specific models**, and the Chief Architect's work is to draw that line.
results.finding: Declared problem_solution carrying 'failures a single brand can make' and introducing 'the group decisions that prevent them'. The opening does not pick up the failure modes just listed or present the group view as what prevents them; it starts a new framing (squad feature vs platform).

All other declared transitions are expressed at their boundaries (e.g. 'The consequence is a design principle', 'Evaluation says what to optimize; consent and law say what may be used', 'Beyond these trade-offs', 'Each failure below breaks one rule of this chapter').

results.quote: Every listing is a cold-start problem, and every recommendation is a bet on an item that may disappear before the buyer clicks.
results.finding: Cold start is on audience.does_not_know. It is used in the opening, the scope paragraph ('This chapter owns ... cold start') and 'It is the cold-start backbone', but defined only in Cold Start in Three Forms ¶1, several sections later.
results.corroborated_by: flow_A item 3c ('cold start is used from the lead ... but defined only at ...'); flow_B item 3b

results.draft_locus: Cold Start in Three Forms, table, new market row
results.quote: Tradeyard's new cargo-bike leaf from November 2027
results.finding: 'Leaf' (a leaf of the category tree) is used without explanation and is not in audience.already_knows.
results.corroborated_by: flow_A item 3l ('"Leaf" ... is jargon here'); flow_B item 3k ('"Leaf" (a category-tree leaf) is not explained')

results.quote: When the Lyon apartment's three agency listings are clustered into one canonical property, the recommender must choose one listing to show.
results.finding: 'The Lyon apartment' is referred to with a definite article as if known; already_knows lists entity-resolution clusters and the Essen Golf but not this example, and the chapter never introduces it.
results.corroborated_by: flow_A item 3p ('this chapter does not introduce it'); flow_B item 3q

results.quote: This is the most valuable piece to share, and in Veldmark's case it comes with the Common Ground event backbone.
results.finding: 'Common Ground' is named as if known; it is not on already_knows and the chapter never says what it is beyond the word 'backbone'.
results.corroborated_by: flow_A item 3q ('Common Ground is not explained in this chapter'); flow_B item 3r

results.quote: The candidate sources above already give new listings a place; this section returns to them for the published evidence behind that choice, then covers the two forms the architecture has not yet addressed, new users and new markets.
results.finding: Both readers mark the section's position as partly unclear: the central problem of the chapter is defined and evidenced only after the architecture that solves it, and a third of the section reads as backtracking. The draft now signposts the return exactly as the spec's transition_in declares, and both readers still propose moving the section (or its new-listing evidence) before the Architecture section. The difficulty comes from the declared order (cold start after architecture), not from the prose.
results.corroborated_by: flow_B item 2 (Cold Start in Three Forms: 'Position partly unclear ... a third of it is backtracking') and item 4; flow_A item 2 ('position somewhat unclear') and item 4

results.quote: Vinted and Airbnb made the same trade-off and settled it differently, because their inventory lives for different lengths of time.
results.finding: 'The same trade-off' is never named (freshness of the item side against serving cost), and the Vinted bullet is mostly about rebuilds, pre-filtering and exact vs approximate search, so both readers re-read the sentence.

results.quote: It had a good run: **23 leads in 10 days** (raw leads; 19 after deduplicating repeat contacts from the same buyers), a price cut to **€21,400** on 22 April that triggered price-drop alerts to 1,180 watchers, and a sale at 15:10 on Thursday **29 April**.
results.finding: Reader B re-read this dense sentence of numbers to find the point (the 26-hour removal lag); the deduplication aside is not used again. One reader only.

results.finding: Reader B found the paid-placement aside sudden, since paid placement had not come up in the chapter. One reader only.

results.quote: Motorvane stays on Elasticsearch 8 until the 2029 search review, so the design uses what that engine provides rather than waiting for the group platform.
results.finding: Reader B: 'the group platform' and, in the same unit, 'the listing event contract v1' are used as if known; the shared OpenSearch platform is described only later. One reader only.

results.quote: Evaluation says what to optimize; consent and law say what may be used.
results.finding: Reader B marks the section's position 'somewhat unclear': it separates Evaluating Recommendations from the rebuild whose table uses its metrics. Reader A found the position clear (reordering 'minor; the current order works'). One reader only; the spec's rationale (evaluation must precede the rebuild, privacy limits the whole) holds.
Opens on the kettle/Golf contrast (intriguing example) and a claim; none of the weak patterns.
Synthesis plus hand-off; no 'in conclusion', no new subtopic, no body evidence, not a bare restated thesis.

Ties content sources, events/one status filter and contact measurement to one fact (the item is new, unique and about to go) and gives the so-what: a group sharing the status read model and event stream gets most of the gain before any model is trained.
'The kettle recommender fails on listings because the item is new, unique and about to go' returns to the kettle, the Golf and the bet on an item that may disappear.

The intro reader predicted every section in order (scene, surfaces, why listings break, methods, four stages with events, cold start, feedback loops, evaluation, consent and regulation, the Motorvane rebuild, then trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, Chief Architect's view, questions), the evidence (published marketplace case studies, EU regulation, Veldmark numbers) and the tone.

The AC-1 reader gives the four candidate sources (attribute similarity, embeddings with a content tower, co-contact every two hours, fresh nearby listings), events within a minute, one serving-time filter on the shared status read model with trust/duplicate/already-contacted rules, a lead-trained GBDT re-ranker with position correction, a policy with a dealer-group cap and an exploration slot, judgment on leads with coverage as a guardrail while click-through falls 4%, and the sale-to-removal gap closed at the source (mark-as-sold, 15-minute feed contract).
